**STEP 1 – Scene:** A single whole citrus fruit, either an orange or a large mandarin, sitting on an otherwise empty plate. It is a snack rather than a full meal.

**STEP 2 – Vessel:** A white square plate with rounded corners, about 22 cm across. That gives an area of about 22 × 22 ≈ 480 cm² (a square, so the circle formula doesn't apply).

**STEP 3 – Items:** One whole unpeeled orange. There is no oil or sauce.

**STEP 4 – Area:** The orange is about 128 px wide and the plate about 345 px, so the orange is roughly 8 cm in diameter. Its footprint is 3.14 × 4² ≈ 50 cm², about 10% of the plate. Food covers about 10% of the plate in total.

**STEP 5 – Volume:** For a whole fruit, treat it as a sphere rather than area × height. An 8 cm sphere has a volume of 4/3 × 3.14 × 4³ ≈ 268 ml. The fruit looks slightly flattened, so I take about 220 ml.

**STEP 6 – Grams:** 220 ml × 0.8 (whole citrus, including the slightly lighter peel) ≈ 175 g. I'll use 170 g.

**STEP 7 – Energy:** About 47 kcal per 100 g for orange flesh. Since the peel is included in the weight, I use a blended value of about 42 kcal per 100 g. 170 g × 0.42 ≈ 71 kcal.

**STEP 8 – Sanity check:** A medium-to-large orange typically weighs 150–200 g and has 60–80 kcal, so the estimate is plausible.
